posts.title: This Week at Blackwood
posts.excerpt: The Crossing enters ARC circulation, the Blackwood Circle opens further, and the house prepares for September.
posts.body:
This week at Blackwood has been centred on The Crossing by Miren Vale, which is now moving into the hands of advance readers ahead of publication on 14 September. ARC readers have been contacted, and the first stage of the release is now underway as we begin gathering early responses and preparing the book for its arrival in the wider catalogue.

The Blackwood Circle is also beginning to take on a larger role within the house. It is becoming the place where readers can build their Blackwood record, collect points, follow new publications and receive selected notices from the archive. Approved ARC readers will also receive access to a separate advance-reading area within the Circle, with access issued individually for each reader.

Behind the scenes, work continues on the systems that allow Blackwood Publishing to grow beyond a single author and into a working independent press. That means developing the reader programme, organising ARC access, refining catalogue presentation, strengthening direct editions and continuing conversations with booksellers. The Black Bothy is currently with Waterstones St Andrews for consideration following the arrival of review copies, while further bookseller outreach continues around the Scottish catalogue.

September will belong largely to The Crossing. Over the coming weeks we will be following the ARC response, preparing publication material and introducing more of Miren Vale’s novel before its release. The book opens with an invitation hidden inside an unmarked library book and leads towards a ruined chapel, an old ritual and a crossing shaped by memory, silence and the cost of being noticed.

Alongside the release, work will continue on the wider Blackwood catalogue and on the structure behind the house itself. The aim remains simple: each publication should feel connected to something larger, with readers able to move from one book, record or author into another part of the archive.

More will be issued as September approaches.

posts.title: The Crossing ARC Now Open
posts.excerpt: ARC interest is now open for The Crossing by Miren Vale, a dark literary fantasy of memory, silence, ritual, and the places we are warned not to enter.
posts.body:
The Crossing ARC is now open.

Blackwood Publishing is preparing advance digital reader copies for The Crossing by Miren Vale, a dark literary fantasy of memory, silence, ritual, old bargains, and the places we are warned not to enter.

The Crossing follows Isla after she opens an unmarked library book and finds her name written inside a sealed letter. By morning, the road is recognised by people who should not know it, an old rule has returned, and the crossing has begun.

This is a book for readers drawn to threshold places, family silence, buried knowledge, coastal ruin, ritual, and the moment ordinary landscape begins to reveal what has always been present beneath it.

ARC copies will be supplied digitally. Reviews are always expected to be honest. There is no requirement to leave a positive review.

Readers who would like to be considered for The Crossing or future Blackwood ARC opportunities can apply through the ARC Team page under the Community tab.

Not every invitation is sent, some are answered.

posts.title: The Archive Begins to Move
posts.excerpt: A quiet but important week inside the archive: Holdfast reached Hot New Releases, the Circle opened, direct orders moved, and Martin Hales’ next release began taking shape.
posts.body:
This week at Blackwood has been one of those weeks where the archive began to feel less like a collection of books and more like a living system.

Holdfast, Book Four of The Archive Files, reached #4 in Amazon Hot New Releases in its category. That was a small but meaningful moment. The Archive Files began with The Black Bothy, a missing sister, a final recording, and a remote Highland bothy and now the fourth book is finding its way to readers.

The full Archive Files sequence is now available:

The Black Bothy
The Drowned Fjord
The Erased Archivist
Holdfast

Signed paperbacks and the full signed bundle are also available direct from Blackwood Publishing. Direct orders have started moving steadily, and every signed copy sent out from the Blackwood store helps keep this small press growing.

The Blackwood Circle has also opened properly.

This private reader area is where reader records, ARC updates, rewards, member dispatches, early notes, and behind-the-book fragments will gather. It is not just a mailing list. It is a place for returning readers, early supporters, reviewers, collectors, and anyone who wants to follow Blackwood from inside the archive.

Martin Hales is also moving quietly in the background.

His practical finance books are already being read through Kindle Unlimited, and work has begun on The Money Reset, planned for a December release. The idea is simple: read the book in December, then use the companion workbook to begin your reset in January.

The Money Reset will be built around a five-stage framework:

Reveal
Essentials
Stabilise
Establish
Take Control

It will also be supported by a practical spreadsheet workbook, designed to help readers record their key money numbers, organise debts, plan irregular costs, build sinking funds, review subscriptions, and complete a 30-day money reset.

Miren Vale’s The Crossing is also being finalised for its September release. This will be Blackwood’s next fiction doorway: dark literary fantasy, threshold places, old bargains, memory, loss, and the cost of stepping where you were never meant to go.

So the shape of Blackwood is becoming clearer now.

Aidan Blackwood for atmosphere, horror, grief, memory and place.
Miren Vale for dark literary fantasy and gothic threshold fiction.
Martin Hales for practical, calm, useful finance guides.

Three lines. One press. One growing archive.

Thank you for being here at the start of the Circle.

Leave a record.
Return when the archive calls.

posts.title: Miren Vale: The Crossing Opens Next
posts.excerpt: The Crossing by Miren Vale is being finalised for its September release, with ARC invitations, BookFunnel delivery, and early reader notes planned before launch.
posts.body:
The next fiction doorway at Blackwood belongs to Miren Vale.

The Crossing is now being finalised for its September release. This will be Miren’s first Blackwood title: a dark literary fantasy about threshold places, old bargains, memory, loss, and the cost of stepping where you were never meant to go.

It is not part of The Archive Files or The Cursed Bothies.

It opens a different door.

Over the next few weeks, the focus will be on final polish, ARC preparation, early reader copies, and launch materials. Selected ARC readers will receive digital advance copies through BookFunnel before publication. As always with Blackwood ARCs, reviews are expected to be honest. There is no requirement to leave a positive review.

The current plan is:

Finalise the manuscript and cover details.
Prepare the BookFunnel ARC file.
Select suitable ARC readers from the Blackwood ARC Team.
Send early digital copies.
Gather early reader notes and review links where available.
Prepare launch posts, product pages, and release-week material.

The Crossing is planned for release on 14 September 2026.

For readers already inside the Circle, this means you will begin seeing more of Miren Vale here before the wider launch campaign begins: fragments, mood notes, ARC updates, and behind-the-scenes pieces from the making of the book.

Miren’s line at Blackwood will sit beside Aidan Blackwood’s atmospheric horror and Martin Hales’ practical guides, but it has its own shape: dark literary fantasy, gothic atmosphere, impossible thresholds, old stories, and the unsettling question of what waits on the other side of a choice.

A new Blackwood voice.
A new doorway.
The same quiet unease.

The crossing opens next.
